title: Rapid RTLS Deployment Support for a New Hospital Tower
summary: See how CBIZ's FAIR team delivered RFID tagging and a validated asset baseline for a 1.9M sq. ft. hospital tower RTLS rollout on a tight timeline.
body_markdown:
## Issue


A leading healthcare Real Time Location Systems (RTLS) partner required support for a growing hospital client preparing to open a newly constructed tower. The 1.9 million-square-foot facility included 820 private rooms and 234 ICU beds, and approximately 13,300 target medical equipment assets needed to be located, validated, and RFID tagged before the tower opened in three months. Timing was critical because the baseline inventory had to be completed and prepared for the partner’s software before the final onsite RTLS installation and tower rollout.


## Solution


The Fixed Asset Inventory & Reconciliation (FAIR) team, part of the Tangible Asset Practice (TAP) within the CBIZ Valuation Group (CVG), immediately assembled an experienced healthcare inventory team led by a partner-experienced, PMP-certified project manager serving as the single point of contact. The project manager was supported by permanent FAIR field staff, site leads, quality control, administration, and logistics resources sized to meet the compressed opening schedule.


The FAIR team inventoried medical equipment staged throughout patient rooms, operating rooms, and storage areas; captured the required asset tag, description, manufacturer, model, serial number, building, floor, room, and department information; and affixed RFID asset tags in locations consistent with partner and hospital requirements. The FAIR team also updated the partner-provided asset import list, coordinated changes to the standard inventory sweep and site completion process, and prepared the validated baseline inventory for loading into the company’s software.


Using proprietary toolsets, FAIR’s quality control team reviewed field data daily for missing asset tags, upload verification, location and asset accuracy, demographic duplicates, model and serial number exceptions, duplicate serial numbers, and inconsistent description-manufacturer-model combinations. Daily and weekly reporting provided visibility into inventory progression and asset counts by description, manufacturer, model, and floor.


## Outcome


The FAIR team provided the project management structure, field capacity, and daily data controls needed to establish a validated baseline inventory for the new tower. The completed asset information and RFID tagging supported loading the baseline into the company’s software for use during the RTLS rollout, while daily reporting gave the partner and hospital project leads continued visibility into production, data compliance, and readiness for final installation.By combining rapid mobilization, PMP-certified project leadership, healthcare inventory experience, disciplined RFID tagging procedures, and daily quality control, FAIR operated as an extension of its RTLS partner during a time-sensitive hospital expansion. The engagement demonstrates FAIR’s ability to help healthcare technology partners meet fixed go-live commitments, establish reliable baseline asset data, and support successful RTLS deployments in complex clinical environments.
